system: civil law system based on the Roman-Dutch model and influenced by customary law

constitution.history: drafted July to August 1945, effective 18 August 1945, abrogated by 1949 and 1950 constitutions; 1945 constitution restored 5 July 1959
constitution.amend: proposed by the People's Consultative Assembly, with at least two thirds of its members present; passage requires simple majority vote by the Assembly membership; constitutional articles on the unitary form of the state cannot be amended

courts.highest: Supreme Court or Mahkamah Agung (51 judges divided into 8 chambers); Constitutional Court or Mahkamah Konstitusi (consists of 9 judges)
courts.judges: Supreme Court judges nominated by Judicial Commission, appointed by president with concurrence of parliament; judges serve until retirement at age 65; Constitutional Court judges - 3 nominated by president, 3 by Supreme Court, and 3 by parliament; judges appointed by the president; judges serve until mandatory retirement at age 70
courts.lower: High Courts of Appeal, district courts, religious courts

citizenship.descent: at least one parent must be a citizen of Indonesia

suffrage: 17 years of age; universal; married persons regardless of age
world: has not submitted an ICJ jurisdiction declaration; non-party state to the ICCt
